newsitem.title: GERMANY: Unstoppable German DAX sets fresh records.
newsitem.headline: Unstoppable German DAX sets fresh records.

text.p: German shares extended Monday's sharp gains to surge to fresh records in early trade on Tuesday, shrugging off a wobbly start by Bunds and cheered on by some well-received corporate earnings.
Although the rally ebbed after a spurt in the pre-bourse session, many dealers said the market appeared healthy and ripe for more gains in the short term.

The blue chip DAX index was up 19.11 points at a record 3,676.97 points, boosted by gains of nearly four percent on retailer Metro AG and nearly two percent on steelmaker Thyssen AG on the back of strong profit reports.
"Those were excellent numbers, not only from Thyssen but also from Metro," said a dealer.
"That was a real surprise and an added boost for the market in the morning."

Metro shares hit an alltime high of 189.90 marks in pre-bourse trade and were up six marks at 184 in bourse dealings after it reported its first group profit on ordinary activities of 1.1 billion marks in 1996.
Thyssen hit a high of 404 marks before settling back to trade up seven marks, or 1.8 percent, at 399.50 marks after it reported an 81 percent rise in first half pre-tax profit.
Overall, prices were well off the day's highs in bourse trade, after the IBIS DAX index hit an alltime high of 3,691.56 points during electronic dealings.
"We need calm after the past two days," a dealer said of the slowdown. "This is a healthy sign in a market."
